label: ALTER COLLECTION ENABLE/DISABLE ANALYTICS
type: the DDL statement mapping a Data-service collection into Analytics (or removing that mapping) - equivalent to CREATE ANALYTICS SCOPE + CREATE ANALYTICS COLLECTION (enable) or DROP ANALYTICS COLLECTION (+ DROP ANALYTICS SYNONYM if needed) (disable). Also performable through analytics:workbench's 'Map From Data Service' UI action - the statement and the UI action are two surfaces for one operation, stated directly on the management page.
aliases_note: Folds a genre fork of the same shape rounds 18-20 kept finding: a DDL reference page (5_ddl.md, and this round's worked-example page primer-beer.md) minted analytics:alter-collection-statement, while a management-guide page (manage-datasets.md, a different batch, dispatched concurrently with no visibility into the other) minted the shorter analytics:alter-collection for the identical statement. 2 files vs 1, zero overlap, 3 combined. Kept the longer, more specific spelling as canonical because 5_ddl.md's own naming convention reserves the bare CRUD-verb form (create-analytics-collection, drop-analytics-index) for statements whose object noun disambiguates them, and uses a `-statement` suffix specifically for the four statements whose bare name would otherwise be a generic word (ALTER, CONNECT, DISCONNECT, USE) - alter-collection alone reads as an English phrase, not obviously a SQL++ statement id.
evidence: This is equivalent to running CREATE ANALYTICS SCOPE followed by CREATE ANALYTICS COLLECTION.
This is equivalent to running DROP ANALYTICS COLLECTION, and if necessary DROP ANALYTICS SYNONYM.
You can also map collections from the Data service using the ALTER COLLECTION statement.
relates_to_competency_question: Can an existing Data-service collection be mapped into Analytics after the fact, and is that a UI action, a DDL statement, or both?
